evidence: gpt-oss-120b uses “adj = [0] * n”, “1 << v”, and a “depth-first search for an independent set of size k”; the statement gives “1 ≤ n ≤ 46”
secondary_shortcut_name: early acceptance of any valid witness
removal_suggestion: The numeric bound cannot be removed under the constraints. To reduce this shortcut indirectly, replace “Any group in which no two users are connected is accepted” with a canonical-witness requirement such as requiring the lexicographically smallest valid group, forcing the solver to continue after finding the first witness.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses integer bitmasks and branch-and-bound-style DFS, which is practical for a graph of at most 46 vertices and can stop at the first valid group.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: 1 ≤ n ≤ 46; “Any group in which no two users are connected is accepted.”

common_affordance: The small fixed maximum of 46 vertices makes exact independent-set search with Python integer bitmasks and DFS feasible.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its backtracking search remains exponential on adversarial instances and timed out despite using bitmasks.
It enumerates all k-combinations and checks every pair, giving an especially large combinatorial search and timing out.
It relies on greedy minimum-degree selection rather than an exact independent-set search, so the method has no correctness guarantee; the submitted implementation also produced a runtime error.

recommended_edit: Because the 46-vertex bound is immutable, change the acceptance wording from allowing any valid group to requiring a canonical valid group, such as the lexicographically smallest one. This removes the survivor's ability to stop at the first DFS witness and requires substantially more search.
regression_risk: This may restore the already-defeated exhaustive-combination solver only if the new canonical-witness requirement is implemented with unusually weak tests; otherwise it makes that approach even slower.
